requirements.requirement: Create the sharedops identity with UID and GID 4200 on all three nodes, and set /srv/nfs/shared to sharedops:sharedops mode 2770.
requirements.summary: Direct identity checks show UID/GID 4200 on node1, node2, and node3. Final server and client views agree that the shared directory is owned by sharedops:sharedops and has mode 2770.

requirements.requirement: Operate node1 as an NFSv4 server exporting /srv/nfs/shared read-write to node2 and node3 over the dedicated storage network.
requirements.summary: The nodes use 10.100.150.10-12 on the storage subnet. Node1's active, enabled server exports the requested path specifically to client addresses .11 and .12, and serves NFS on port 2049. A server restart changed its boot identity, after which the service, export, files, and both client connections recovered.

requirements.requirement: Mount node1:/srv/nfs/shared at /mnt/shared on both node2 and node3.
requirements.summary: Both clients show active NFSv4.2 mounts at /mnt/shared sourced from node1's storage address, with persistent fstab entries. Each client recovered the mount, identity, and existing data after its own restart.

requirements.requirement: Make files created from either client immediately available from the other while retaining ownership and permissions.
requirements.summary: Node2 created a UID/GID 4200 mode-0640 file that node3 immediately read with matching metadata; node3 likewise created a mode-0660 file that node2 immediately read. Final server and client observations show matching ownership, modes, contents, and hashes for all proof files.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for every node: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, mount, identity, data, and cross-node behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently match all pre- and post-restart identities.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified, so none remained or required reversion. Package installation, identities, export configuration, mounts, bounded proof files, and restarts all had direct roles in the task or mandatory restart protocol. The partially failing export command retained only the required shared directory and was completed successfully; the failed proof commands created or flushed bounded evidence data later verified successfully. Final snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, and no abandoned apt evidence files in /tmp.
